newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to sell heavy bombers to Russia.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to sell heavy bombers to Russia.

text.p: Ukraine has agreed in principle to sell 25 strategic heavy bombers to Russia though terms have yet to be finalised, the defence ministry said on Tuesday.
Spokesman Valery Korol told Reuters the defence ministries had agreed the sale and purchase of 10 "Blackjacks" -- or Tupolev-160s -- and 15 Tu-95s.

The planes, which can carry nuclear bombs and missiles over a long range but have not flown since the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, would be paid for in cash, spare parts and debt relief, defence sources said.
Russia also wants to buy 800 cruise missiles from Ukraine which can be used with the aircraft, but the entire deal would have to get government approval first, the sources added.
Russian news agencies have said Kiev had accepted an offer of $320-$350 million for the planes but Korol denied this.
"This figure is Russia's proposal. The experts are about to finalise the price," Korol said.
He also denied that the planes were in need of repairs, saying: "They can fly as we have been spending almost $1 million a year to keep them in an acceptable condition".
Russian experts have been quoted as saying only a third of the planes were in a fit state to fly missions.
Defence officials said Russia would pay some of the cost in spare parts for Ukraine's military aircraft and by reducing Ukraine's huge energy debt to Moscow.
